extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, administrative law researchers, agency officials, and statisticians studying federal adjudication timing and hearing-examiner workload
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the timing- and workload-related metrics used in a government report (tables) summarizing federal agencies' adjudicative proceedings (hearing completion intervals, time from examiner decision to final decision, time under advisement, and examiner backlog) for fiscal years in the late 1950s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time interval from commencement of proceeding to completion of hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Table heading: 'TIME INTERVAL FROM COMMENCEMENT OF PROCEEDING TO COMPLETION OF HEARING (CASES CLOSED BY AGENCY FINAL DECISION IN FISCAL 1959)'. Rows are 'KINDS OF PROCEEDINGS REPORTED BY THE AGENCIES' and showing per-kind counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported columns (time buckets): 'Hearing completed in 3 mos. or less'; 'Over 3 months but not over 6'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Over 1 year but not over 2'; 'Over 2 years'. Each row shows 'Cases closed by final decision' and distribution across those buckets. Examples of proceeding kinds appear by agency (e.g., Atomic Energy Commission—'Constr. permit & facil. lie.', 'Byproduct material license'; Civil Aeronautics Board—'Route licensing', 'Foreign permits', etc.). Averages by category are sometimes reported (e.g., 'Average 2.7 months'). Footnotes indicate exclusions and missing time data for some categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time interval from examiner's decision to agency final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Table heading: 'TABLE 6 - TIME INTERVAL FROM EXAMINER'S DECISION TO AGENCY FINAL DECISION (PROCEEDINGS TERMINATED IN FISCAL 1959 BY AGENCY FINAL DECISION ON THE MERITS AFTER AN EXAMINER'S DECISION)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported columns (time buckets): 'Agency decision in 3 mos. or less'; 'Over 3 months but not over 6'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Over 1 year but not over 2'; 'Over 2 years'. Rows list kinds of proceedings by agency with counts in each bucket. Footnotes clarify cases where time data are not available and other exclusions (e.g., 'Time data not available', 'Excludes 16 Indian probate matters').

rubrics_metrics.name: Time under advisement by the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Table heading: 'TABLE 7 - TIME UNDER ADVISEMENT BY THE AGENCY'. Presents counts of cases 'Under advisement' for specified time intervals for fiscal years 1958 and 1959.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported columns: total cases closed by final decision, then 'Under advisement 1 month or less'; 'Over 1 month but not over 3'; 'Over 3 months but not over 6'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Under advisement more than 1 year'. For each bucket the table provides 1958 and 1959 counts. Rows are kinds of proceedings by agency. Footnotes note missing data and exclusions (e.g., 'The 1959 grand totals exclude 517 Social Security cases and 2,033 Interstate Commerce Commission cases for which these data are not available').

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of proceedings pending before hearing examiners (workload/backlog)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table heading: 'TABLE 8 - NUMBER OF PROCEEDINGS PENDING BEFORE HEARING EXAMINERS DURING THE FISCAL YEARS 1957, 1958, AND 1959'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns: 'Pending before examiners at the beginning of the year' (1957,1958,1959); 'New cases assigned to examiners during the fiscal year' (1957,1958,1959); 'Old cases remanded or reassigned during the fiscal year' (1957,1958,1959); 'Number disposed of by examiners during the fiscal year' (1957,1958,1959); 'Pending before examiners at the end of the year' (1957,1958,1959). Rows are kinds of proceedings reported by agencies. The table gives counts by year and by proceeding type, enabling analysis of examiner caseload flow (inflow, dispositions, backlog).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of proceedings reported by the agencies (proceeding categories / docket types)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report enumerates many agency-specific proceeding kinds (the row labels used in the tables), often with statutory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (verbatim or close to page wording) include: 'Constr. permit & facil. lie., 42 USC 2134, 2235, 2239(a)'; 'Byproduct material license, 42 USC 2111, 2231, 2239(a)'; 'Order to show cause, 42 USC 2231, 2236, 2239(a)'; 'Route licensing, 49 USC 1371'; 'Broadcast licensing, 47 USC 309,312,316,325,405'; 'Cease & desist orders, 15 USC 13,21,45,68d,69f,1194'; 'Appeals from benefit rights determinations, 42 USC 405'; 'Certificates of convenience and necess., 49 USC ...'; 'Indian probate matters, 25 USC 372,373'; 'Walsh-Healey Act enforcement, 41 USC 39'; etc. These proceeding kinds serve as categorical dimensions for reporting timing and workload metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time interval metrics (aggregate summary averages)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tables sometimes report average durations for particular categories or overall (e.g., 'Average 2.7 months', 'Average 7.8 months', 'Average 6.9 months', 'Average 8.1 months').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averages accompany the bucketed distributions to summarize typical durations for hearings or post-examiner decisions; footnotes indicate that some averages exclude certain agency data where not available ('Grand total figures exclude 1,233 Interstate Commerce Commission cases, 517 Social Security cases, and 16 Indian probate matters, for which information for this table is not available'). Use caution interpreting averages because of excluded subsets and missing data notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes and data caveats (exclusions, missing data, special conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple footnotes accompany the tables, noting exclusions, missing data, and special counting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of footnote content: '26 non-hearing safety enforcement proceedings ... are excluded from this table'; 'Time data not available'; 'Excludes 16 Indian probate matters for which information is not available'; 'Grand total figures exclude 1,233 Interstate Commerce Commission cases, 517 Social Security cases, and 16 Indian probate matters ...'; 'Includes periods during which these cases were suspended awaiting determination of the Communist Party, U.S.A. case.' These caveats affect completeness and comparability of reported counts and averages and should be considered when using the metrics.
